added.title: VP, Software Delivery
added.description:
Who We Are...

Verra Mobility is a global leader in smart mobility. We develop technology-enabled solutions that help the world move safely and easily. We are fostering the development of safe cities, working with police departments and municipalities to install over 4,000 red-light, speed, and school bus stop arm safety cameras across North America. We are also creating smart roadways, serving the world's largest commercial fleets and rental car companies to manage tolling transactions and violations for over 8.5 million vehicles. And we are a leading provider of connected systems, processing nearly 165 million transactions each year across 50+ individual tolling authorities.

Culture

Verra Mobility Corporation is a dynamic, entrepreneurial company that operates with a people-first philosophy and approach. The company lives by its core values—Do What’s Right, Choose Courage Over Comfort, Win Together, and Own It—in everything it does for its customers and team members. The company seeks to grow, both organically and through acquisition, to continue to be the undisputed market leader with a bias for action, customer focus, teamwork, drive for results, and commitment to excellence.

Position Overview

The VP of Software Delivery owns software delivery outcomes across the Platform, Credential, and Violations portfolios. This is the senior technical delivery leader for the domestic organization, accountable for predictable, high quality delivery at scale, and for the multi year cloud modernization strategy that moves the company's legacy systems onto resilient, cloud native architecture.

You will be the organization's foremost authority on how to modernize legacy platforms while delivering customer centric solutions that incrementally replace legacy capability with cloud native services. You will bring the financial acumen to defend that roadmap in dollars and risk, the Agile fluency to run delivery at a pace the business can trust, and the customer centric instinct to keep the entire department focused on outcomes that matter to the people who use what we build.

Essential Responsibilities

Software Delivery Leadership

Portfolio Oversight: Own end to end delivery outcomes across the appointed leader of each portfolio and their squads, including roadmap commitments, release predictability, quality, and operational stability.
Business Outcomes: Understand how each portfolio's feature roadmap connects to actual business outcomes, such as revenue, customer retention, and cost to serve, and hold each portfolio's appointed leader accountable to outcomes rather than output shipped.
DORA Metrics: Track deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, and time to restore service across every squad, and understand what each metric signals about a squad's underlying health, not just its current number.
Quality Strategy & Automation: Be well versed in delivering quality outcomes and in quality automation strategy, and know how to adapt that strategy for teams that include few or no dedicated software engineers, such as field hardware, operations, or support functions, so quality practices extend across the full delivery organization rather than only the teams already staffed for it.
Portfolio Leader Development: Personally evaluate and develop the appointed leader of each portfolio, ensuring each is functioning as the technical subject matter expert their portfolio needs, and act decisively through coaching, role redefinition, or personnel change when one is not. Read heartbeat delivery metrics, such as sprint predictability, cycle time, and escaped defects, as an early signal of squad or leader health, and use that signal to decide when the right response is coaching, mentoring, closer management, or replacement.
Delivery Standards: Set the delivery operating standards, from planning cadence to release management to production readiness, that apply consistently across all three portfolios, while allowing legitimate portfolio specific variation.

Cloud Architecture & Modernization Strategy

Strangler Pattern Migrations: Own the enterprise strategy for incrementally replacing legacy systems with cloud native services using strangler fig style migration, sequencing cutover to protect existing customers and revenue while retiring legacy platforms on a defined timeline.
Cloud Solution Architecture: Serve as the organization's cloud solution architecture authority, designing for horizontal scale and resiliency, and partnering with the Senior Enterprise Architect to keep migration decisions consistent with enterprise standards.
PaaS vs. IaaS Strategy: Set clear, defensible criteria for when a workload belongs on Platform as a Service versus Infrastructure as a Service, weighing operational overhead, control, cost at scale, and time to market for each portfolio's workloads.
Resiliency & Scale: Draw on a hands on software development background and fluency in modern architecture patterns to ensure migrated and net new systems are engineered for high performance and high availability at the scale this business runs at, often millions of backend transactions per day, while still delivering a modern, responsive experience for front end users.
Architecture & Delivery Assessment: Be technical enough to personally assess both architecture decisions and delivery execution, not just review status reports, so the organization's technical choices and the way they are actually delivered both hold up against recognized industry standards.
Market Awareness: Maintain current knowledge of technical solutions and vendors available in the market, so build versus buy decisions and architecture choices are informed by what already exists rather than by what the internal team happens to know.

Financial Stewardship

Migration Business Case: Build and defend the financial case for cloud modernization investment, including total cost of ownership comparisons between legacy operating cost and cloud native run cost, and the return on migration investment over time.
Budget Ownership: Own the delivery organization's budget across the three portfolios, making trade off calls between run, migrate, and build investment that the business can defend.
Bid & Contract Review: Own final review and approval of technical bids and contracts for the domestic delivery organization, ensuring commitments are achievable within existing architecture, governance, and cost constraints before they are signed.

Agile Delivery & Customer Centricity

Agile Operating Model: Champion Agile practices and a consistent delivery cadence across all three portfolios, coaching portfolio leaders and Managers on removing impediments rather than adding process for its own sake.
Customer Centricity Mentorship: Personally mentor the department on customer centricity principles, ensuring squads validate real customer problems before building and measure success in customer and business outcomes, not just output shipped.
Cross VP Partnership: Partner with the VP, Innovation and Emerging Technology and the VP, International Portfolio to keep delivery standards, cloud architecture decisions, and customer centric practices consistent across the full engineering organization.

Qualifications

Experience: 12+ years in software engineering or technology delivery leadership, with at least 6 years at the senior director, VP, or equivalent level leading multiple teams or portfolios through other leaders.
Business Outcome Fluency: Demonstrated ability to connect feature level delivery to business outcomes such as revenue, retention, and cost to serve, and to redirect a team's roadmap when its output is not moving the outcomes that matter.
Education: A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience is required; an advanced degree or MBA is a plus given the financial scope of this role.
Financial Acumen: Demonstrated ability to build, defend, and manage a technology budget and investment case, including total cost of ownership analysis and return on investment modeling for major infrastructure decisions.
Domain Knowledge: Experience in mobility, tolling, government technology, or other transaction heavy, compliance sensitive industries is strongly preferred.

Verra Mobility Values

An ideal candidate for this role naturally works in alignment with the Verra Mobility Core Values:

Own It: We focus on high performance and drive toward breakthrough outcomes. Our employees ensure accountability, optimize and align work, focus on the customer, and cultivate innovation.
Do What’s Right: We champion integrity and good character. Our team members model ethical behavior, demonstrate good judgment and are courageous.
Choose Courage Over Comfort: We lean into the conversations, decisions and actions that move the business forward, even when they feel uncomfortable. We challenge assumptions, address issues early and prioritize progress over ease.
Win Together: We believe in growing and inspiring people together. We seek people who collaborate, value differences, think and act globally, foster an engaging work environment, and recognize and develop others.

added.title: VP, International Software Delivery
added.description:
Who We Are...

Verra Mobility is a global leader in smart mobility. We develop technology-enabled solutions that help the world move safely and easily. We are fostering the development of safe cities, working with police departments and municipalities to install over 4,000 red-light, speed, and school bus stop arm safety cameras across North America. We are also creating smart roadways, serving the world's largest commercial fleets and rental car companies to manage tolling transactions and violations for over 8.5 million vehicles. And we are a leading provider of connected systems, processing nearly 165 million transactions each year across 50+ individual tolling authorities.

Culture

Verra Mobility Corporation is a dynamic, entrepreneurial company that operates with a people-first philosophy and approach. The company lives by its core values—Do What’s Right, Choose Courage Over Comfort, Win Together, and Own It—in everything it does for its customers and team members. The company seeks to grow, both organically and through acquisition, to continue to be the undisputed market leader with a bias for action, customer focus, teamwork, drive for results, and commitment to excellence.

Position Overview

The VP, International Portfolio owns the Automated Enforcement and Tolls and Violations portfolios cradle to grave across the international business, reporting to the SVP, Software Engineering. Cradle to grave ownership means full accountability for each portfolio's technology, delivery, support, and P&L, not delivery alone. Because customer relationships in this business often span more than one region, this role also owns the coordination model for any shared or overlapping regional coverage, ensuring accountability stays clear even when a single account touches multiple markets.

This is one of the most operationally demanding roles in the organization, requiring a leader who can run a coherent global business across regions that never share a full working day. You will set the strategy for how the organization leads across time zones, ensure every local leader has deep, current fluency in the specific regulatory and commercial realities of their own market, and hold each business accountable for its own P&L while keeping both portfolios coherent under a single technology and delivery strategy.

Essential Responsibilities

Global Portfolio & P&L Ownership

Cradle to Grave Accountability: Own Automated Enforcement and Tolls and Violations end to end, including technology strategy, delivery, production support, and full profit and loss accountability for each portfolio.
Appointed Portfolio Leadership: Ensure each portfolio has an appointed leader who is the true technical and commercial owner of their business, evaluating and developing those leaders directly and acting decisively when a leader is not performing at the level the role requires.
Cross Region Coordination: Own the coordination model between APAC and European operations, ensuring accountability, support coverage, and commercial ownership stay unambiguous wherever the two regional organizations' work overlaps.
Support Ownership: Own the international support organization as part of the portfolio's full lifecycle accountability, ensuring support coverage spans global operations rather than a single region, and operates on a model that matches how the business actually runs across time zones.

Cross Region Leadership Across Time Zones

Global Operating Rhythm: Design and run a deliberate operating cadence, including meeting timing, decision rights, and asynchronous communication norms, that lets APAC and European teams collaborate effectively despite little or no overlapping working hours.
Follow the Sun Coordination: Establish handoff practices for support, incident response, and delivery work that needs continuous coverage across regions, so critical issues do not stall waiting for a single time zone to wake up.
Travel & Presence Strategy: Maintain a deliberate in person presence strategy across both regions, recognizing that relationship building, culture setting, and complex negotiation in these markets often require being there rather than dialing in.

Local Market Enablement

Local Leader Fluency: Ensure the appointed leader in each region has deep, current fluency in their own market's regulatory environment, customer expectations, and competitive landscape, rather than relying on this role as the sole source of market context.
Distinct Go to Market Models: Allow each business to operate with the go to market and service model its market actually requires, resisting the temptation to force a single global template where local realities genuinely differ.
Regulatory & Compliance Awareness: Maintain working knowledge of how government procurement, data privacy, and automated enforcement regulation differ across APAC markets, Europe, and the UK, sufficient to know where a single compliance approach will not transfer.

Enterprise Coherence & Partnership

Technology Alignment: Draw on a hands on software development background and fluency in modern architecture patterns to partner credibly with the VP, Software Delivery and the Senior Enterprise Architect, ensuring the international portfolios' systems are engineered for high performance and high availability at the transaction volumes these businesses actually process, often millions of backend transactions per day, while still delivering a modern, responsive experience for front end users, and that technology and delivery standards stay consistent with the domestic organization even where go to market and support models diverge.
Cross VP Partnership: Partner with the VP, Innovation and Emerging Technology and the VP, Software Delivery to ensure new capabilities and delivery standards developed domestically extend cleanly into the international portfolios where relevant.
Executive Reporting: Report portfolio health, P&L performance, and regional risk clearly and regularly to the SVP, Software Engineering and executive stakeholders, translating operational complexity into a coherent business narrative.

We Are Looking For a Leader Who Can Run a Genuinely Global Business, Not Just a Domestic One With International Customers

Global Operating Leadership

A proven ability to lead effectively across regions and time zones with little or no overlapping working hours, without collapsing into either constant after hours availability or regional disconnection.

P&L Ownership

Real, demonstrated accountability for a business's financial performance, not only its technology or delivery outcomes.

Cross Cultural Fluency

Genuine comfort operating across different business cultures and regulatory environments, and the humility to let local leaders own the nuance of their own markets.

Portfolio Breadth

Comfort owning a full portfolio lifecycle, from technology strategy through production support, rather than a single slice of the value chain.

Qualifications

Experience: 12+ years in technology or product leadership roles, with at least 5 years owning an international or multi region business with direct profit and loss accountability.
Education: A bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience is required; an MBA or equivalent is a plus given the P&L scope of this role.
Global Leadership: Demonstrated success leading teams and businesses across multiple regions and time zones, including establishing an operating rhythm that keeps distant teams genuinely aligned rather than nominally connected.
P&L Management: Direct experience owning a business unit or portfolio's profit and loss, including pricing, cost management, and investment trade off decisions made with real financial accountability.
Regulatory Breadth: Working knowledge of how government procurement, data privacy, and automated enforcement or tolling regulation vary across APAC, European, and UK markets.
Domain Knowledge: Experience in automated enforcement, tolling, violations processing, or other government facing, transaction heavy technology businesses is strongly preferred.
Talent Development: A track record of identifying, developing, and holding accountable strong local leaders, and the judgment to know when a portfolio's success depends on stepping back rather than directing from a distance.
Travel Readiness: Willingness and ability to travel regularly and extensively across APAC and Europe, given the relationship and market dependent nature of this role.

Verra Mobility Values

An ideal candidate for this role naturally works in alignment with the Verra Mobility Core Values:

Own It. We focus on high performance and drive toward breakthrough outcomes. Our employees ensure accountability, optimize and align work, focus on the customer, and cultivate innovation.
Do What’s Right. We champion integrity and good character. Our team members model ethical behavior, demonstrate good judgment and are courageous.
Choose Courage Over Comfort. We lean into the conversations, decisions and actions that move the business forward, even when they feel uncomfortable. We challenge assumptions, address issues early and prioritize progress over ease.
Win Together. We believe in growing and inspiring people together. We seek people who collaborate, value differences, think and act globally, foster an engaging work environment, and recognize and develop others.

added.title: Vice President of Engineering
added.description:
The Company

Frontline Data Solutions provides web-based environmental, health, and safety software to some of the world's leading chemical, oil & gas, and manufacturing companies. Frontline is a fully distributed organization, and all roles, including this one, can be performed from any location within the United States. Frontline is unique in that it combines the fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment of a start-up software company with the stability and reputation that reflects its 27-year history of serving blue-chip industrial customers.

Frontline has 50 full-time employees, including approximately 30 full-time Engineering team members. Unlike most tech companies of this size, we have operated independently for more than 20 years and are not controlled by VC or PE investors

A s Vice President of Engineeri
ng, you will lead our engineering organization, owning product delivery, technical direction, and team performance. Reporting to the CTO, you will help shape our technology strategy and drive execution as we scale. Working closely with the CTO and the C-suite leadership team, you will oversee a distributed engineering function, ensuring high-quality delivery across the full technology stack and maintaining the reliability and scalability of our platform.

Frontline is a fully distributed organization, and this role is fully remote.

What You’
ll Do

Ownership :
End-to-end responsibility for the design, development, and delivery of the company’s full suite of web and mobile applications.
Leadership
: Lead, mentor, and develop a distributed team of engineers across software development, DevOps, QA, Design, and Product, working closely alongside our CTO. Direct reports include Engineering Managers and Team Leads.
Performance
: Drive continuous improvement through strong engineering practices, including code reviews, retrospectives, and clear performance management.
Hiring
: Partner with the CTO on engineering hiring strategy, including attracting, onboarding, and developing high-performing talent.
Strategy
: Reports directly to the CTO and works closely with the Executive Team to define technical direction, shape the product roadmap, and align Engineering to business goals.

Candidate Profile

Education
: B.S. Degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Experience
: 5+ years of success managing and scaling software engineering teams.

Skills You’ll Need

Microsoft Stack:
Experience with ASP.NET, .NET Core, and building scalable, API-driven applications within the Microsoft ecosystem (PREFERRED)
Web Stack:
Familiarity with JavaScript, jQuery, JSON, REST APIs, and front-end technologies.
Cloud & Infrastructure
: Strong understanding of Azure services, including App Services, cloud hosting, identity (Azure AD), and modern platform architecture.
Systems
: Experience managing and securing Windows-based environments, including servers, IIS, and core infrastructure.
Backend
: Solid experience with SQL Server and cloud-based database solutions.
Security
: Working knowledge of core security practices, including access control, patching, SSL, and enterprise-grade protection.
Identity
: Experience with Single Sign-On (SSO) and authentication frameworks.

What You'll Get

Exposure
: Direct partnership with senior executives within a growing enterprise SaaS business.
Culture
: Entrepreneurial environment with zero bureaucracy and high ownership.
Progression
: Clear path to executive-level leadership.
Compensation
: Competitive executive package including base salary, performance bonus, equity participation, and benefits.
